front: Internal or external audience decides everything
back: An external agent has no user identity to act as, so anything it can reach is effectively public to every visitor. Keyword: external means public.

front: Shared connection vs user identity
back: A shared connection gives every user identical results regardless of entitlement. Acting as the signed-in user honours the source's own permissions. Keyword: whose permissions apply?

front: Why choose channels early
back: Adaptive cards, file upload, and authentication all behave differently per channel. A topic authored around a rich card may not render where you publish. Keyword: channel decides capability.

front: The single best fix for confident wrong answers
back: Turn off general knowledge so the agent must ground in your sources and says it does not know instead of improvising. Keyword: force grounding.

front: What content moderation actually trades
back: High = conservative, declines more. Low = attempts answers from weaker matches. It is a business decision about wrong answers versus unhelpful ones. Keyword: strictness is a choice.

front: What a DLP policy stops an agent doing
back: It classifies connectors into business and non-business groups, so the connector holding customer data cannot be combined with one that posts to the internet. Keyword: block the exfiltration path.

front: The largest unit of reuse
back: A child agent. Publish the capability as its own agent with its own lifecycle, tests, and owner, and let others delegate to it. Keyword: delegate, do not copy.

front: What belongs in a flow, not a prompt
back: Anything that must happen the same way every time. The model decides what the user wants; the flow does the deterministic part. Keyword: exact logic is not a prompt.

front: Why parameter descriptions are load-bearing
back: The orchestrator reads names and descriptions to decide when a flow applies and what to pass. 'input1' with no description gets called at the wrong moments. Keyword: descriptions are code.

front: Long-running back end in an agent flow
back: Raising the timeout is not the fix. Acknowledge, start the work, return the result later — the asynchronous or human-in-the-loop pattern. Keyword: do not make the user wait.

front: What human-in-the-loop is for
back: Any action that spends money, changes an entitlement, or contacts a customer. The agent proposes, a named human disposes, the approval is recorded. Keyword: consequential means approved.

front: Unhandled flow error inside a conversation
back: Produces a generic apology and no diagnosis, so the user just asks again. Use run-after to return a meaningful output the topic can react to. Keyword: fail usefully.

front: Classic vs generative orchestration
back: Classic matches trigger phrases to one authored topic. Generative lets the model choose and combine topics, tools, and knowledge. Keyword: matched, or chosen.

front: What the generative answers node does
back: The retrieval-augmented step: searches configured knowledge and answers from what it finds. Its key setting is whether it may add general knowledge. Keyword: RAG in a node.

front: When not to use an adaptive card
back: When the answer has no structure and needs no action. Overusing cards makes the agent feel like the form it was meant to replace. Keyword: cards for structure only.

front: Send HTTP request vs custom connector
back: Send HTTP request is fastest and least governed — fine for a one-off. Anything reused, or needing managed auth and DLP classification, belongs in a custom connector. Keyword: reuse means connector.

front: Variable scope in a conversation
back: Topic variables live in their topic, global variables span the session, system variables expose the user and conversation. Crossing topics needs global or an input. Keyword: topic scope does not travel.

front: Why Copilot connectors for enterprise content
back: They index into the Microsoft 365 semantic index and respect the source's own permissions, so each user sees only what they could see in the source. Keyword: indexed and trimmed.

front: Knowledge source or action connector?
back: 'What does our content say about X' is knowledge and needs an index. 'What is the status of order 4471' is an action against a live system. Keyword: written down, or looked up.

front: When Azure AI Search earns its cost
back: When chunking, ranking, or filtering must be controlled directly — custom analysers, hybrid and vector search, your own metadata. Keyword: control the retrieval.

front: Right documents, wrong passages
back: That is a chunking and ranking problem, not a content problem. Point generative answers at your own Azure AI Search index through Foundry. Keyword: fix retrieval, not content.

front: Why computer use is the last resort
back: It depends on the target's visual layout, so a redesign, a new consent dialog, or a slow page breaks it. Keyword: no contract, only pixels.

front: The integration preference order
back: Official connector, then REST API or custom connector, then computer use only when neither exists. Keyword: UI automation is last.

front: What an agent driving a UI can access
back: Everything the account it signs in as can access. Scope those credentials to exactly the task. Keyword: computer use inherits the account.

front: What makes MCP different from adding actions
back: Connecting one server adds every tool it publishes at once, and the agent picks up new tools as the server adds them without being re-authored. Keyword: the tool set is dynamic.

front: Why an MCP server is a trust boundary
back: Someone else may control which tools your agent gains. Use a server you run or have vetted, scope its credentials, and cover it with DLP. Keyword: dynamic means trusted.

front: What a custom connector buys over a raw call
back: Managed authentication, a place in DLP classification, and reuse across agents, apps, and flows. Keyword: governance and reuse.

front: The API auth decision that leaks data
back: Using one stored connection for an API that returns per-user data. Act on behalf of the signed-in user whenever the caller might not be entitled to everything. Keyword: service or user?

front: Where to draw multi-agent boundaries
back: By ownership and lifecycle. The team that owns expenses owns the expenses agent, tests it, and ships it on its own cadence. Keyword: split by owner.

front: Why splitting improves answer quality
back: Generative orchestration degrades as it chooses among more tools with overlapping descriptions. Delegation shrinks the parent's choice set. Keyword: fewer, clearer options.

front: Delegation does not carry permissions
back: A child agent has its own knowledge configuration and connection identities, so routing through a parent can return different results. Keyword: align auth across agents.

front: Copilot Studio or Foundry?
back: Copilot Studio for fast assembly with governed connectors. Foundry when you need a specific model, custom orchestration, or its evaluation tooling. Keyword: speed or control.

front: Knowledge source vs Fabric data agent
back: A knowledge source retrieves passages someone wrote down. A data agent generates and runs queries to compute an answer nobody wrote down. Keyword: retrieve or compute.

front: "What did we sell in the north-west last quarter"
back: A Fabric data agent question — the answer must be computed from data, not retrieved from a document. Keyword: aggregates are computed.

front: What A2A adds
back: An open protocol letting agents discover and call one another across platforms and vendors via published agent cards. Keyword: cross-vendor delegation.

front: Why choose a model from the Foundry catalogue
back: It makes capability, latency, cost, and data residency an explicit decision. A reasoning-heavy step and a short summary do not need the same model. Keyword: model choice is a design choice.

front: Built-in analytics vs Application Insights
back: Analytics answers 'how is the agent doing' — resolved, escalated, abandoned. Application Insights answers 'why', by correlating with the back ends. Keyword: outcome or cause.

front: Why descriptions matter on REST tools
back: Under generative orchestration the model picks tools by name and description. 'Does the thing' gets invoked unpredictably. Keyword: describe when it applies.

front: Copilot connector permission trimming
back: Results are trimmed to what the asking user may see in the source system, which is why they suit content with real access control. Keyword: the index respects ACLs.

front: Why test sets matter more for agents
back: Behaviour is not deterministic. A change to an instruction, a source, or a model can improve one class of question and quietly degrade another. Keyword: nothing announces a regression.

front: What a test set actually is
back: Inputs with expected outcomes, run to produce a measurable result rather than an impression. Keyword: measure, do not eyeball.

front: When exact matching is not enough
back: Open-ended answers with no single expected string. Use model-graded evaluation on groundedness, relevance, and completeness. Keyword: grade, do not compare.

front: The practical evaluation arrangement
back: Automated evaluation on every change, human review of the disagreements. Humans stay the arbiter where it matters. Keyword: automate the bulk, review the edges.

front: How to read evaluation results
back: By comparison. One run tells you little; the same set before and after a change tells you what the change did. Keyword: deltas, not absolutes.

front: What a falling groundedness score means
back: The measurable form of the agent starting to answer from the model instead of your content. Watch it whenever knowledge configuration changes. Keyword: groundedness tracks drift.

front: An agent built outside a solution
back: Has to be added retrospectively, which is where its flows, connectors, and knowledge configurations get left behind. Keyword: start inside the solution.

front: Exporting a multi-agent solution
back: Check dependencies — flows, custom connectors, prompts, and child agents. A parent without its children imports as a parent that delegates to nothing. Keyword: children are dependencies.

front: What environment variables protect you from
back: A test environment pointing at production knowledge sources and API addresses. Those are exactly the values that must differ. Keyword: externalise the endpoints.

front: A missing environment variable value
back: Does not fail loudly. The solution imports and the component behaves as misconfigured, because it is. Supply values in the pipeline, not by hand. Keyword: silent misconfiguration.

front: Extending Power Platform pipelines
back: Add approvals before a stage, or call out to Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions, when governance needs a gate the built-in pipeline lacks. Keyword: extend rather than abandon.
